test.title: A TV series you enjoyed watching

document.cue: Describe a TV series you enjoyed watching.

text: I'd like to talk about a British detective series called 'Broadchurch'. I watched it last winter, all three seasons, mostly on my laptop in the evenings after work, and I think I finished the first season in about four days, which says a lot.

It's set in a small seaside town in the south of England, where a young boy is found dead on the beach. Two detectives are sent to investigate: a local woman who knows everyone and a tired, grumpy inspector from outside who trusts nobody. Their relationship is almost as interesting as the crime itself.

What surprised me was how slowly the story develops. Each episode focuses on a different family or neighbour, and you gradually realise that almost everyone in the town has a secret. There's one scene where the whole community gathers on the cliffs at night with candles, and it's filmed so beautifully that I watched it twice.

I enjoyed it because it's not really about who committed the crime. It's about how a tragedy affects a community where people thought they knew each other. The acting is excellent, and it also helped my English, because I watched it with English subtitles and learned a lot of informal British expressions.
It's one of the few series I'd happily watch again from the beginning.
